description: Foundations of efficiency and complexity analysis

slides.title: Why Learn DSA? 🏗️
slides.content:
# The Foundation

Data Structures and Algorithms (DSA) are the building blocks of efficient software.

- **Data Structure**: A way to organize data (e.g., Array, Graph).
- **Algorithm**: A step-by-step procedure to solve a problem (e.g., Sorting).

## Importance
1. **Performance**: Efficient code saves money (server costs) and time (user experience).
2. **Scalability**: What works for 10 users might fail for 10 million.
3. **Interviews**: The standard metric for assessing problem-solving skills at Google, Amazon, etc.

slides.title: Big-O Notation
slides.content:
# Big-O Notation 📈

Big-O describes the **upper bound** of an algorithm's growth rate. How does runtime increase as input size (n) increases?

| Notation | Name | Speed |
|---|---|---|
| **O(1)** | Constant | Instant regardless of n |
| **O(log n)** | Logarithmic | Very fast (Binary Search) |
| **O(n)** | Linear | Proportional to n (Loop) |
| **O(n log n)** | Linearithmic | Good sorting (Merge Sort) |
| **O(n²)** | Quadratic | Slow (Nested loops) |
| **O(2ⁿ)** | Exponential | Impossible for large n |

> 💡 **Tip**: Always aim for O(n) or O(n log n)!

slides.title: Complexity Quiz
slides.quizQuestion: Which complexity is worst (slowest) for large inputs?

slides.title: Time vs Space
slides.content:
# Trade-offs ⚖️

Software engineering is about trade-offs.

## Time Complexity
How fast does it run? CPU cycles.

## Space Complexity
How much memory (RAM) does it use?

**Example**: You can make an algorithm faster (Time ↓) by storing intermediate results in a Hash Map (Space ↑). This is the **Time-Space Trade-off**.

slides.title: Amortized Analysis
slides.content:
# Amortized Analysis 📊

Sometimes an operation is slow once, but fast most other times.

**Example**: Appending to a Python list (Dynamic Array).
- Usually **O(1)**: Just add to the end.
- Rarely **O(n)**: The array is full, so Python creates a bigger array and copies all elements.

Because the heavy copy happens rarely, the **average** (amortized) time is still O(1).
